brief: Morgan Stanley says a perfect storm - resilient growth, sticky inflation, energy-market disruption, a newly hawkish Fed, heavy corporate issuance, persistent fiscal deficits and a less predictable Treasury - has pushed 2y/5y/10y Treasury yields up 120-150bp since March. After the Fed's 25bp September hike, markets price almost 100bp more tightening; MS's baseline sees only two more hikes (75bp total), holding through end-2027, so its weighted-average path stays below market pricing until after 1Q27. MS sees no near-term fundamental catalyst - inflation progress, a Middle East resolution, or decelerating AI-related capex - that would shift markets dovish, so hawkish sentiment likely persists. Separately, the report tracks a seventh-month oil shock it treats as a permanent risk premium: WTI $96.41 and Brent $114.89 (Sept 22), SPR at 284.6mn barrels (lowest since 1984, approaching its ~70mn operational floor by March 2027 at the current drawdown pace), and a widening diesel-crude gap tied to Strait of Hormuz refinery disruptions. It also updates tariff tracking (effective rate 6.7% May-July, seen converging toward 10% by year-end) and previews the week's GDP, employment, PCE and ISM data.
